title: A power series ring over a Noetherian normal domain is a Noetherian normal domain
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and let $R[[x]]$ be the ring of formal power series in one variable $x$ over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] (the case $n=1$). Then $R[[x]]$ is a Noetherian normal domain: it is Noetherian, an integral domain, and every element of its fraction field which is a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients in $R[[x]]$ lies in $R[[x]]$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0BI0 (lemma-power-series-over-Noetherian-normal-domain), lines 8149-8174, statement and proof (Laurent series over the fraction field, Lemma almost-integral)

proof.text: $R[[x]]$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-noetherian] (case $n=1$), and it is an integral domain by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-domain] (case $d=1$), since $R$ is a domain. In particular its field of fractions $\operatorname{Frac}(R[[x]])$ is defined, and the normality to be shown is: every $w\in\operatorname{Frac}(R[[x]])$ integral over $R[[x]]$ lies in $R[[x]]$ [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0BI0 (lemma-power-series-over-Noetherian-normal-domain), lines 8156-8159: 'The power series ring is Noetherian by Lemma lemma-Noetherian-power-series (0306). Let $f, g \in R[[x]]$ be nonzero elements such that $w = f/g$ is integral over $R[[x]]$.' (the source does not mention that $R[[x]]$ is a domain; it is needed for $f/g$ to make sense)

proof.text: Let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$. The coefficientwise inclusion $R[[x]]\to K[[x]]$ followed by the inclusion $K[[x]]\to K((x))$ of [def-weil-pbc-laurent-series] is an injective ring homomorphism $\iota\colon R[[x]]\to K((x))$ (both maps keep all coefficients and $R\to K$ is injective); its image is the set of Laurent series $\sum_ia_ix^i$ with $a_i\in R$ for all $i$ and $a_i=0$ for $i<0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-laurent-series-field], $K((x))$ is a field, so by [lem-weil-pbc-fraction-field-lift] applied to the domain $A=R[[x]]$ (step 1) and $g=\iota$, $\iota$ extends to an injective ring homomorphism $\tilde\iota\colon\operatorname{Frac}(R[[x]])\to K((x))$. For $u\in\operatorname{Frac}(R[[x]])$ we write $\tilde\iota(u)=\sum_ia_ix^i$ with $a_i\in K$, and for $u\ne0$ this is $a_nx^n+a_{n+1}x^{n+1}+\cdots$ with $n\in\mathbf Z$ its order and $a_n\neq0$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0BI0 (lemma-power-series-over-Noetherian-normal-domain), lines 8160-8163: 'Let $K$ be the fraction field of $R$. Since the ring of Laurent series $K((x)) = K[[x]][1/x]$ is a field, we can write $w = a_n x^n + a_{n+1}x^{n+1} + \ldots$ for some $n \in \mathbf{Z}$, $a_i \in K$, and $a_n \neq 0$.'

proof.text: The image of an integral w under the lift j is integral over K[[x]] by IsIntegral.map_of_comp_eq. Mathlib PowerSeries.instUniqueFactorizationMonoid (PowerSeries/Inverse.lean:285) and UniqueFactorizationMonoid.instIsIntegrallyClosed (Polynomial/RationalRoot.lean:139) supply normality of K[[x]]; this is the field power-series specialization of the normality tool [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal]. LaurentSeries.instIsFractionRingPowerSeries (LaurentSeries.lean:298) identifies K((x)) as its fraction field. IsIntegrallyClosed.algebraMap_eq_of_integral therefore gives a power series f over K whose Laurent image is j(w). This replaces the negative-order calculation by existing proved Mathlib instances.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0BI0 (lemma-power-series-over-Noetherian-normal-domain), lines 8149-8174, statement and proof (Laurent series over the fraction field, Lemma almost-integral)

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-almost-integral-integral] to obtain a nonzero h in R[[x]] with h*w^e in R[[x]] for every e. Apply j and use injectivity of the power-series inclusion to transport this witness to f. To prove the lowest-coefficient claim, suppose the coefficients of f below n vanish, and factor f=X^n*g using PowerSeries.X_pow_dvd_iff. Write m=order(h) and h=X^m*h.divXPowOrder. Expanding h*f^e factors out X^(m+n*e); its coefficient in that degree equals b*(coeff n f)^e, where b=coeff m h is nonzero. Every such coefficient is the coefficient of a power series over R, so coeff n f is almost integral over R [def-weil-pbc-almost-integral]. Noetherianity and [lem-weil-pbc-almost-integral-integral] make it integral, and [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] gives a preimage in R. This is proved by the private helper coeff_almostIntegral, including the case coeff n f=0.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0BI0 (lemma-power-series-over-Noetherian-normal-domain), lines 8164-8170: 'By Lemma lemma-almost-integral (00GX) we see there exists a nonzero element $h = b_m x^m + \ldots$ in $R[[x]]$ with $b_m \neq 0$ such that $w^e h \in R[[x]]$ for all $e \geq 1$. We conclude that $n \geq 0$ and that $b_m a_n^e \in R$ for all $e \geq 1$. Since $R$ is Noetherian this implies that $a_n \in R$ by the same lemma.' (the last sentence also uses that $R$ is normal: 00GX gives integrality, normality gives membership)

proof.text: Strongly induct on n. For i<n choose preimages r_i in R supplied by the induction hypotheses, and put p=sum_{i<n} r_i X^i. The series f-map(p) has zero coefficients below n and its n-th coefficient equals that of f. The subalgebra completeIntegralClosure from [def-weil-pbc-almost-integral] contains both f and map(p), hence their difference. Apply the lowest-coefficient calculation of the preceding step, convert almost integrality to integrality over the Noetherian R, and use normality. This proves that every coefficient of f has a preimage in R (private helper coeff_mem_range). Only proved preimage statements are used in the choices.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0BI0 (lemma-power-series-over-Noetherian-normal-domain), lines 8170-8173: 'Now, if $a_n, a_{n+1}, \ldots, a_{N-1} \in R$, then we can apply the same argument to $w - a_n x^n - \ldots - a_{N-1} x^{N-1} = a_N x^N + \ldots$. In this way we see that all $a_i \in R$' (the source leaves implicit that $w - a_nx^n - \ldots$ is again integral over $R[[x]]$, which is the subring property of integral elements)

proof.text: Choose r_n in R with algebraMap(r_n)=coeff n f and form g=PowerSeries.mk(r_n). Coefficientwise extensionality proves map(g)=f. Its Laurent image is j(w), and injectivity of j gives algebraMap(g)=w. Together with Noetherianity and the domain instance this proves the required conjunction.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0BI0 (lemma-power-series-over-Noetherian-normal-domain), line 8173: 'In this way we see that all $a_i \in R$ and the lemma is proved.'
